question:
A 33-year-old woman arrives at the emergency department after a motor vehicle accident with
significant blood loss reported by emergency medical personnel. Her husband provides her medical
history, noting that she has eczema, recurrent sinus infections, and chronic diarrhea, along with a 10-lb
weight loss over the past few months. A prior work-up revealed a negative stool culture and negative
anti-transglutaminase test. She takes no medications. On examination, the patient is conscious but in
pain, with a large laceration on her right thigh. Imaging of the right lower extremity shows no fractures,
and exploration of the wound reveals no nerve or major artery damage. A focused sonographic

assessment is negative. Laceration repair is performed. Laboratory results show: Hemoglobin: 6.7 g/dL
Hematocrit: 27% Leukocyte count: 6,000 cells/mm³ (normal differential) Platelet count: 200,000/mm³
The patient receives a red blood cell transfusion, after which she develops dyspnea, urticaria, and
hypotension. A chest radiograph is normal. Which of the following conditions is most likely associated
with this clinical presentation? Answer Choices: (A) Hereditary Angioedema (B) Selective IgA
Deficiency (C) Systemic Mastocytosis (D) Febrile nonhemolytic transfusion reaction (E) Inflammatory
Bowel Disease (F) Common Variable Immunodeficiency (G) Chronic Eosinophilic Gastroenteritis (H)
Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome (I) Transfusion related acute lung injury (J) Celiac disease
 A. Systemic Mastocytosis
B. Febrile nonhemolytic transfusion reaction
C. Inflammatory Bowel Disease
D. Selective IgA Deficiency
E. Common Variable Immunodeficiency
F. Chronic Eosinophilic Gastroenteritis
G. Hereditary Angioedema
H. Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome
I. Celiac disease
J. Transfusion related acute lung injury
